reading.body:
Four of the six tools tracked here, CrowdStrike Charlotte AI, Darktrace, Palo Alto Networks Precision AI, and SentinelOne Purple AI, are noted for autonomous response, meaning the AI does not just flag a threat but can act on the network directly.

That is a different risk profile than most AI tools on this site, where the worst case is bad output. Here the worst case is bad action, an autonomous response system that misidentifies a threat can lock out legitimate users, quarantine production systems, or cut off network segments on its own. SentinelOne's note specifically flags kill-switch capabilities, which implies the vendor itself treats an off-switch as a necessary control rather than a footnote. Okta AI is the outlier in this group, focused on identity and risk-based authentication rather than network defense, and Zscaler AI focuses on inspecting traffic and preventing data loss rather than autonomous action.

Darktrace is the one UK-hosted, GDPR-relevant vendor in the group, while the other five are US-based. The data does not say how often these autonomous response features are enabled by default versus opt-in, or how frequently they trigger falsely, only that the capability exists and is treated as a defining feature of this category.
